notes.title: Switching to Godot & Changing The Art Style
notes.content:
[h1]Dear Elyndrans![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/ac2037dfe4126ca7b211b63d1562b32c17858b7a.png[/img]
We’ve decided to change the engine and the art style of Call of Elyndra. We will use Godot and combine pixel art sprites with 3D environments. This marks a huge shift for the game. We have more planned. Read on to find out.

[h2]The Decision[/h2]

Ever since we announced the game, we’ve mostly seen enthusiasm and excitement. Call of Elyndra is a beautiful game. It’s also a lot of fun. Those who have played the demo know that already. Still, some have pointed out some things that could have been improved. The framerate, the game feel, the ease of work, possible quality enhancements… Plenty of room for improvement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/feb1d2d973ef43453187e03ca9eb106078fa16a2.jpg[/img]
Our huge strength and also the biggest hindrance was the engine. RPG Maker is a phenomenal bit of software, and there are some masterpieces of gaming made with it. Some of our team members are also known in the RPG Maker community. At first, we wanted to make the most technically advanced game in the engine, which we may have achieved as RPG Maker makes up only about 30% of our code. Our team has long gone past the predetermined boundaries. We made the engine do things that it shouldn’t have been able to do. Alas, it still wasn’t enough. Some of the inherent solutions and limitations simply couldn’t be helped. Also, the looks, while quite beautiful, could have been improved upon. There are many games with stunning pixel art and we knew that we needed to shake it up a bit.

[h2]The Engine[/h2]

Godot is becoming an increasingly popular choice for game studios. It has a bunch of features that indie teams, like us, are looking for. It’s free, open source, and allows for a huge degree of customisation and freedom. Luckily, our team is made up of very gifted individuals. They were able to either adapt or remake the vast majority of mechanics and code in the new engine. If the game is a success, we’ll also have an easier time with porting it to other platforms. Not saying it’s something that’ll happen, but it could, if enough people are interested.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/9c07332943c9db0326bddc691dfa397288027ac5.png[/img]
A huge part of Godot is that it is able to use 3D quite well. Now, about that…

[h2]The Art Style[/h2]

There are so many beautiful classic games. Call of Elyndra draws a lot of inspiration from them. Still, since Call of Elyndra is a contemporary title, we felt that presenting it in the style reminiscent of 2DHD of Octopath Traveller, Dragon Quest 3 Remaster, Live A Live, and a couple of other games is the right call. Juxtaposing our beautiful sprites against 3D environments will make them pop even more. On the technical side, the game should perform even better now since RPG Maker renders visuals using the CPU and Godot uses GPU processing, superior in terms of efficiency and performance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/92d9b157bf1bd885861bb1d2958228a4db7183a6.png[/img]
In regards to gameplay, the new art style allows us to create more interesting environments. After all, we’ll be able to use verticality for exploration, combat and puzzles.

[h2]Plans and Summary[/h2]

We’ll be revealing more stuff here and on our social media in the future. We also plan a new version of the demo, so keep an eye out for it as well. The development of the full version should take us more time than we previously expected, but we’re on track and quite happy with where we are. Our understanding of the current circumstances is good. We know what to do to make Call of Elyndra as good as it can be, and we’re committed to getting it right.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/878787ed1c727f993507145d32a45e550d10a207.png[/img]
Thanks for reading, talk to you again soon!

notes.title: Devlog #5 - Farming
notes.content:
[h1]Hey Elyndrans![/h1]

We’ve mostly talked about the game’s story and action in our devlogs so far, but this time we want to focus on something different - farming. Since you can choose between going on quests or working the land, let’s dive into the farming side of things!

[h2]The Basics[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/df3f49517b9e829beefe4bf32e0ff708bbc2fcc9.gif[/img]
If you’ve tried the demo, you know that farming is pretty simple. Just follow these steps:

[list]
[b][*] Till the land to make tiles.
[*] Sow the seeds.
[*] Water them a few times.
[*] Harvest.
[*] Repeat.[/b]
[/list]
You’ve also got a few easy-to-use tools. To make farming smoother and more enjoyable, you don’t need to switch equipment every time you want to do something different. Just hit the space bar to get things done - except for watering, which demands clicking and holding your left mouse button. It's possible we'll change that in the future. You can sell what you harvest, and some items might also be useful for crafting.

[h2]The Details[/h2]

Farming is pretty chill, and you can take it easy while making progress. But we know some of you want to be as efficient as possible, and there’s plenty to discover and optimize.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/66ebea783825fd8e343325574a855a2ed8ce6907.gif[/img]

First up, [b]soil deterioration[/b]. If you overwork the land, it might get mushy or barren. Right now, this happens randomly, but we might tweak it based on your feedback. We’re also thinking about adding more depth to the system - like factoring in fertilizing, watering, and planting the same crop repeatedly.

To fix mushy soil, just sprinkle some gypsum on it. It shouldn’t happen often during regular gameplay, but it’s good to keep some gypsum around just in case. This will help keep your fields looking nice and productive.

Next, [b]plant synergies[/b]. Just like in real gardening, some plants grow better together. For example, basil helps keep pests away from tomatoes, while tomatoes give basil shade and support. Radishes loosen the soil and attract bugs that eat pests on lettuce. We’re working on similar pairings in the game that will boost your crop yields. We haven’t decided yet how you’ll discover these combos - maybe through experimenting or other in-game hints. Got any ideas? Let us know!

We’re also thinking about adding crop rotation and other farming mechanics, but [b]it all depends[/b] on how the game develops and what players want. We don’t want to pile on features that might not get used, so we’ll see how things go.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/49ecfa4d9e9645f0162abac5bd4393fd75c5e87f.gif[/img]

---

We hope you enjoyed this look into farming in Call of Elyndra. Some players might even make it their main gameplay focus, so we wanted to give it some attention. There’s a lot more to explore, like advancing the story through farming, and we’ll cover that in future updates.

Also, stay tuned for some big news coming soon! If everything goes as planned, we’ll be making a huge announcement. Keep an eye out - you won’t want to miss it!

notes.title: Devlog #4 - Skill Trees
notes.content:
[h1]Dear Elyndrans![/h1]

We’ve been working hard on the game for quite a while now, and we’ve realised there is a need for a huge change. More on that in the near future. Let’s talk about something that hasn’t been mentioned too much. Namely, some of the RPG progression systems we have in the game.

[h2]How will the progression work?[/h2]

If you have played the demo, you have probably seen “mining levelled up!” pop-ups and the likes. Plenty of them, too. Fighting, harvesting, mining… They can be levelled up. How? We wanted to keep that system simple, so you simply have to fulfil these actions to gain experience and then level up. A bit like in Skyrim!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/f5fbe84f7ce2da28c69b40a190bda832274ac4d2.png[/img]

We decided to go in this direction because it seemed the most sensible and seamless. We hold our inspirations, like old JRPGs, dear to our hearts. Still, we know the industry and standards have progressed in gaming over the years. Allocating stat points doesn’t feel right in a game that’s in huge part an action game. Allocating stat points would be great in slower, turn-based games. Instead of going with Final Fantasy, though, we opted for a system similar to Skyrim’s.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/67d8237778b64ce7fd5e7f66ec31a5a5a44c74c2.png[/img]

[h2]Skill trees[/h2]

Call of Elyndra will be in huge part about expressing your playstyle. If you prioritise close-quarters combat, you’ll obviously want to level that part of your character’s skills up. However, making numbers higher doesn’t feel like it’s quite enough. This is why we will have skill trees. You will be able to unlock new abilities and perks that will make your character better at this particular activity. Simple as!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/20eadf6d7dccb523761d1ae66e187667ef17bdde.png[/img]

[h2]Rare earth minerals and all that[/h2]

The game will be filled with resources. Using the rarer ones will be, for the most part, optional. However, some will require better tools to source and harvest. How to come across those better tools? You’ll either need to:
[list]
[*] Craft them.
[*] Find them in dungeons and the overworld.
[*] Buy them from the village.
[/list]
Of course, the game will put you in many different biomes, so you’ll get to explore areas that are going to be filled with rarer resources. Even if you decide just to focus on farming, you will always be able to go to other places and get your resources for crafting there. Kind of like how some people who live in cities go to forests and forage mushrooms. Aside from the fact that you'll need to actively fight or avoid wildlife.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/170ef03c815b76cdfa5b78ab1c6924705ce0203a.gif[/img]

[h2]What are the big changes about?[/h2]

We’ve been talking about those big changes coming to the project. And believe us - we’d really love to share with you already what they are going to be… But we can’t yet. What we will say, though, is that the game is shaping up beautifully. It will certainly be better on all fronts than we first expected and there’s a lot to wait for. We also have a decent idea of when the game will be released and how to proceed with the development. It’s all good, even though extremely intensive. Keep your fingers crossed for us and eyes peeled!

Ah, one more thing. Those are the animation frames of the roll dash of the female MC. It's a cool little piece that demanded a lot of work!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/aada4d1d45fab57854c22a5c84c8e93d1ff115a6.png[/img]

notes.title: Devlog #3 - Let's Make a Monster + More Lore!
notes.content:
[h1]Dear Elyndrans![/h1]

Today’s devlog is going to be [b]mostly about the lore[/b]. The world of Elyndra has plenty of it to uncover. One of our Discord server members told us a while ago that some of the things in the demo didn’t quite make sense to them. Like, why are the villagers dismissive or mean? What’s the deal with The Arconian Empire? We’ll talk about some important concepts in this entry!

[b]This post is spoiler-heavy, but it mostly features early-game stuff[/b]. If you’ve played through the demo, then there shouldn’t be any real big spoilers.

We’re also sprinkling in some nice art pieces and WIPs we have made as of late.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/d5b5b83492bb5c37550661cf08fee67ad2fd13f2.png[/img]

Before we get into that…

[h2]Let's make a monster together![/h2]

Wanna have fun and contribute to Call of Elyndra? [b]Pop in tomorrow, Jan 18th 2025, 2 PM EST, to our [url=discord.gg/invite/TGzGJRmGdQ]Discord server[/url]. We will be hosting an event for the community - let’s design a monster together![/b] Through discussion, democracy, and a bit of craziness, we’ll create something that will become a mob in the full version of the game. We’re talking about both looks and behavior and attacks. 

See you!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/1f2368ec973421da7a7f35eee0bf841c95a10a7d.gif[/img]
[h2]A Good Reason[/h2]

We had been working on the demo for quite a while. Its first version was ready around July. One of the first things that we noticed was that it takes a couple of minutes to get to the point where you start the current demo version. As it’s important to start playing the game as quickly as possible, the start had to be cut. We’re sure it was a good decision… But as a result, some explanations were skipped.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/16cdf13c61d98f8346bc0e552d9579eb713eb437.png[/img]

[h2]Why did you end up in Elyndra? (spoilers ahead)[/h2]

The intro scene shows us the dream that starts the whole endeavour. An entity that we’ll not talk about at this point, bestowed it upon you, Ariadne, and Kaelan. You are thus the Dreamers - ones chosen by destiny (...or maybe something entirely else?) to fulfil a very special task. A task of a more “mystic” and “ethereal” quality.

As the common knowledge says, it’s better not to ignore blatant supernatural signs you’ve seen in your dreams. Thus, you venture to Elyndra - a village on the edge of the civilized world. The place mentioned by the entity.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/49167dd3a83ff262ef5a0e2a9d5eaefbc5772b42.jpg[/img]

[h2]Elyndra’s glorious past (spoilers ahead)[/h2]

Elyndra wasn’t always this middle-of-nowhere it is now. As we mentioned in our previous devlog, it is what was left of a great city, a rich and bustling commerce centre. Due to cataclysms and hardships, the city fell. Its people started forgetting about their great past and their trading ways. The environment and circumstances forced them to live off the land. Some huge ruins nearby paint a bit of the story, but Elyndrans don’t wander there - the area is considered dangerous.

This isolation and simple lives made them self-sufficient, but not very talkative and apprehensive to aliens. This is why you are not exactly welcomed with arms wide open. They treat you and the other 2 dreamers as intruders. It would be hard not to see their point. They also heard that the Empire was making some aggressive moves in other parts of the world. Speaking of which…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/2d4aa0a5e722e796a03fa56eee22c1515a2c73ec.png[/img]

[h2]Arconia and its domination (spoilers ahead)[/h2]

The Arconian Empire is your homeland. It also happens to be the dominant geo-political force in the world. Life there was good. You lived with your mother and thought you’d have a regular imperial citizen’s life. Of course, it turned out differently. In the eyes of The Empire, it didn’t matter much. You were just a speck. It wouldn’t matter anyway soon.

By the end of the demo, Vexaris, the Chancellor of Arconia, waltzes with armed soldiers into Elyndra. This is what empires do. They expand, encroach on other people’s territories, and exploit them. A tale as old as the world itself. However, some questions arise. Why is he so nonchalant when talking about the possible use of violence? Why does Arconia need that backwater village? Are they calculated, just evil, or is there something else at play?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/ab8af83258470ebb1b52cac94128b31e40ea4874.png[/img]

More answers and questions will come in the future.

—

Thanks for reading this entry and for being with us. Have a good one, follow us on social media, and see you soon! Cheers!

notes.title: Devlog #2 - Elyndra's Lore & Our Plans
notes.content:
[h1]Hello![/h1]

It’s been a crazy month for Quorum Games and Call of Elyndra. We’ve seen a lot of support, joy, and hope. We also received a lot of valuable feedback that needs to be introduced to our game.

This post is about our plans for the future. We’ll also talk about Elyndra itself.

[h2]Lore behind Elyndra, the village (light spoilers ahead)[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/d99964e28abfa878648cb5f2d9d8bfac63325a69.png[/img]

Elyndra may look like a regular village at first glance… Second, third, fourth, and so on probably wouldn’t change much. For you, an inhabitant of The Empire, it’s a frontier village like many others. However, [b]there’s a deep history in this place[/b].

Elyndra hasn’t always been known as Elyndra. [b]It used to be something grander[/b] - a municipality called Argentia. It was one of the grandest cities in the whole world. Unfortunately, it fell due to a disaster that obliterated the city and left very few survivors. Even though their home was wiped off the face of the planet, their life had to go on. They wanted to reestablish the city on the ruins of Argentia. It became Elyndra. One could say that the unbreakable will to survive and thrive of these people has become immortalized in the stubborn and resourceful inhabitants of the village.

Unfortunately, [b]life there wasn’t what it used to be[/b]. Waves of emigration thinned out the population and from an almost city, it devolved into a town and then a mere village. With the people, the knowledge and memories also went. Gone were the great technological advancements and high culture. The descendants of those who stayed switched their focus to agriculture. Working the land became the main activity of Elyndrans. They were nowhere as sophisticated as their ancestors, but they could survive in this community.

Now, with the histories of old relegated to the status of mere myths and folk knowledge, Elyndrans live their simple lives. They are also aware of the old and mysterious ruins that lay nearby. Nobody knows what hides there.

Will you venture there and uncover mysteries thought to be lost to time?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/170ef03c815b76cdfa5b78ab1c6924705ce0203a.gif[/img]

Hopefully, you enjoyed that little bit about the lore. Now, let’s move on to the other part of the devlog. 

[h2]Our plans regarding the game's development[/h2]

We’re more or less a month past the game’s announcement and a week after the demo release.

We’ve learned a lot about how people perceive our game. It’s been mostly positive and it makes us quite happy. Our hard work wasn’t in vain and we’re looking with our heads held up high into the future. Still, there are some things we need to work on.

Three areas that universally demanded improvement were:
[list]
[*] [b]The game’s performance.[/b]
[*] [b]Movement and responsiveness of controls.[/b]
[*] [b]Melee combat.[/b]
[/list]
Our focus will definitely be on them. In order to see how our changes are perceived, we expect to update the demo build every few weeks and see what sort of feedback we collect. The reason why we opt for treating our demo a bit like a test build is that it contains most if not all inner workings that the game will have. Code, mechanics, and so on. This effectively means that while we still edit stuff in the engine and write code, we expect to focus on adding content to the game. New areas, monsters, graphics, so on.

In order to do that, we are about to modify some of our internal processes and switch our focus to adding content. We want to expand our team to make more content. The area that demands the most work to be done is animation. All of it is hand-drawn, pixel by pixel. The quality is great, but it takes time and loads of effort. Realistically speaking, we will be able to speed the whole process up and we feel quite good about that aspect.

Something else that demands a lot of work is the inherent stuff caused by RPG Maker, our engine of choice. The engine has a lot of great solutions in its vanilla form. Its big downside is that it is quite limited without customization. We knew that well, as plenty of our team members had worked in RPG Maker before. One of our goals is to create one of if not the most impressive RPG Maker game ever made. And we’ll need to navigate some uncharted waters to do that. Still, we’re quite confident in our ability to make the game as responsive, fluid, and pleasant to play as possible. These things are attainable.

—

We’re about to finish this devlog. As this was only our second, we wanted to talk a huge part about the technical stuff. The future ones will likely be more about the lore and the art. Here’s a quick collage of some of the gifs that our gifted artists have made recently. Some of them are NPCs, some are monsters. All look cool!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/035825b852a6cfbec627aa60a6068169ca3fa9cc.gif[/img]
Thank you for reading. Make sure to follow us on social media and join our Discord!

Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year. 2025 is going to be great!

notes.title: Demo Available NOW!
notes.content:
[h1]Dear Elyndrans![/h1]

[b]Today is the day. Call of Elyndra’s demo is finally available on Steam![/b] You can find it here - [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3170230/Call_of_Elyndra_Demo/]CLICK[/url]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/fb4da0646f281661a0f29716e2c0b79fc30139cc.gif[/img]

In the demo, you will be able to embark on the very beginning of the story in Call of Elyndra. You will get to:
[list]
[*] Clean up the plot of land you will be given and start farming it.
[*] Experience a few days trying to grow as many crops as possible.
[*] Meet the villagers… Will they like your presence there?
[*] Explore the first dungeon - full of enemies, puzzles, and a climactic boss fight by the end of it.
[*] Meet the main characters and the main antagonist of the game.
[*] Learn about your true purpose. You’re the Dreamer, after all.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/49ecfa4d9e9645f0162abac5bd4393fd75c5e87f.gif[/img]

The demo can be finished in between 40 minutes and, from what we’ve seen, up to 2.5 hours. It’s a decent chunk of the game, but still - just the very beginning!

We would like to thank you for being with us and for playing. Stick around, there’s so much more coming!

notes.title: Devlog #1 - Hello World
notes.content:
[h1]Hello World![/h1]

We’re [b]Quorum Games[/b] and you’re reading our first devlog for [b]Call of Elyndra[/b]. Hopefully, you’ll stick around :)

There are also two announcements by the end of it!

[h2]An Overview of Call of Elyndra[/h2]

[previewyoutube=EXXt5f5Ols0;full][/previewyoutube]

So, what exactly is Call of Elyndra? It’s a game that combines 2 genres - cozy farming simulators and oldschool, narrative-driven 2D action RPGs. Think, Stardew Valley meets TLOZ: A Link To The Past. We think that taking the best of both worlds will result in something special… And will allow you to play the game the way you want.

By this, we mean that aside from the introductory stage of the game (which you can experience in the demo LINK) you will have the freedom to focus on [b]questing and fighting[/b], or [b]farming and chilling[/b]. HOWEVER, [b]if you want to do both - you can[/b]. This way, you’ll get the full experience and you’ll satiate both your cozy and adventurous sides.

This game is also pretty different from other cozy games because you can finish it. In a conventional sense, not by just reaching the endgame. Call of Elyndra will feature a cohesive storyline. 

[h2]The story begins…[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/c9ebca359bca11c517fe0cf07348c587a130a338.gif[/img]

One faithful night, you have a dream. It feels more real than anything else you’ve ever dreamed. An otherworldly voice tells you to embark on a voyage to the small village of Elyndra - a middle of nowhere for a citizen of the Empire like you. When you finally arrive there, you meet Ariadne and Kaelan, two young adventurers also brought to the village by the very same dream. The villagers are quite reluctant to accommodate you, but after a discussion, they give you an overgrown plot of land and a ruin of a house. Your task is to prove that you’re worthy to stay there. However, this is only the beginning of the story…

The narrative will have plenty of things to focus on - building relationships, changing convictions, facing an overwhelming enemy force, and plenty of lore. As a matter of fact, we had to substantially scale down what we had wanted to include in our game. At this moment, a 100% playthrough is expected to last for more or less 30+ hours.

[h2]Meet the Elyndrans![/h2]

We mentioned building relationships above. You, as a player character, will control a character you’ll name. So, here’s a little list of some of the most important NPCs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/8399e981322b955d632ed3c3b411f3e52f03dacd.png[/img]

[b]Ariadne [/b]was born into a family of scholars, where books were the best companions and ideas, the greatest weapons. Her analytical mind and observant nature made her both admired and isolated. She was comfortable with her seclusion, preferring the company of her thoughts. However, she carried a secret longing to experience life. She will be one of your main companions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/f0052755637ac16d7faa3331c3aaf992eddfe032.png[/img]

[b]Kaelan [/b]comes from a long line of warriors. From an early age, he was expected to follow this path. The familial expectations molded him into a brash, assertive, and risk-taking individual who jumped headfirst into any situation. However, deep down, he carried a desire to be more than just a warrior, to break free from the constraints of his lineage. He will also be one of your closest companions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/328405fbf54bcccaa5c486b753e8606687ec16d4.png[/img]

[b]Chief Eldon[/b] is the patriarch of the village of Elyndra. An elder but towering figure. He is extremely protective of his people and almost lashes out at most outsiders. The resolve and perseverance he embodies force him to often choose the greater good rather than what he personally prefers. He will be one of the first and most important characters you’ll encounter. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/ab8af83258470ebb1b52cac94128b31e40ea4874.png[/img]

[b]Vexaris[/b], The Chancellor of the Archonian Empire. His brash yet disciplined nature can easily intimidate his subordinates… Not to mention civilians. You’ll get to know him early and he’ll be the man to beat. What secrets does he hold, though?

These few will be quite important along your journey, but you’ll encounter dozens of other characters - all of them with their own opinions, motivations, and such. It will be worth bonding with them because they will be able to assist you in your quests.

[h2]Slash and bash[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/fb4da0646f281661a0f29716e2c0b79fc30139cc.gif[/img]

The combat system will be quite basic in the demo but will be heavily expanded upon in the later versions of the game. Currently, you can:
[list]
[*] swing your sword,
[*] dash,
[*] shoot arrows,
[*] plant bombs.
[/list]
This list will be heavily expanded, though, because there will be two major systems we’d like to talk briefly about.

Items that you’ll find will help you with traversing the terrain and some of them will also help you in combat.

There are also other features and mechanics planned. We’ll see how many of our ideas will make it to the game. We believe that more is better, sure, but we are also realists.

However, not all in this world has to be resolved by conflict, at least not directly by you. You can focus on farming and the cozy stuff.

[h2]Reject the Empire, return to farm[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45307267/49ecfa4d9e9645f0162abac5bd4393fd75c5e87f.gif[/img]

Call of Elyndra allows you to put heavy emphasis on the cozy side of things. You’re handed a plot of overgrown land in the first few minutes of the game. Your goal? To grow enough crops to support the people of Elyndra. And there will be plenty of things to consider before you’ll be able to set up your turnip empire!

The game will have dozens of types of seeds you’ll be able to plant. The demo will feature a couple of them. The full version will have additional mechanics like crop rotations, having some plants grow better in different parts of the year, soil exhaustion, and such. This means that Call of Elyndra will combine the cozy approach and easily understandable mechanics for people who wanna kick back and relax, while also having layers upon layers of things to be figured out if you’d like to maximize your crop output and run the most efficient farmland in the world.

There’s so much more to the farm life than just farming, though. You’ll be able to:
[list]
[*] Tend to animals.
[*] Fish to relax and discover what the bountiful rivers of Elyndra hide.
[*] Build relationships with the villagers and some other people - you’re not alone in this world, after all!
[/list]
And plenty more. So, grab the hatchet and the scythe and start clearing that plot of land, potatoes won’t grow themselves!

[h2]Just a sprinkling of tech stuff[/h2]

While the tech stuff is often overlooked, we have a cool small fact to share.

[list]
[*] The game runs on a heavily modified version of the RPG Maker engine. However, 70% of the code is custom-made. So more than twice the original engine!
[/list]
